game.name: Gunfire Reborn
game.short_description: Gunfire Reborn is a level-based adventure game featuring FPS, Roguelite and RPG. Players can control heroes with various abilities to experience diverse Build gameplay, use various weapons to explore procedurally-generated levels. You can play the game alone, or join 4-player coop.

commentary.label: Tier list Part 1 (2023)
commentary.summary: Gunfire Reborn is a first-person shooter roguelike with multiple characters, weapons, passives and abilities, and it keeps receiving updates. He loves it and calls it packed with content, enjoying it in both single player and multiplayer, though he rates it as a single-player game. He nearly gave it S tier but, after comparing it with other games on the board, settled on high A. He recommends it to shooter fans and advises playing the Steam version over the stale console ones.
praise: Huge amount of content: characters, weapons, passives, abilities, bosses, enemies and game modes
Passive system is enormous, with passives found two to three times per floor so the player constantly feels powerful
Many unique builds and ways to play
Constantly updated with new characters and strong developer support
Also an excellent multiplayer experience with friends
Short floors (often under five minutes) keep the pace brisk
criticism: Runs are very long, up to about an hour and a half for a full run to the final boss
Death means a full restart, so it demands real commitment
Non-Steam versions (Xbox/Microsoft) are not updated and are badly outdated
unique_points: One of the first first-person roguelikes on his board
Frequent passive drops per floor keep the power fantasy going despite long runs
commentary.quote: definitely a high high a tier this game is amazing
design_criteria: Build variety: many unique builds and playstyles
Passives and progression: passive system is huge and frequent
Content volume: many bosses, enemies, modes
Run length: long runs up to 1.5 hours with permadeath restart
Pacing: short floors under five minutes
Ongoing support: frequent updates and new characters
Multiplayer: great co-op, though not scored on it

community.one_liner: A colourful first-person roguelite looter-shooter with RPG-style characters, scroll-based builds and 1-4 player co-op, made by Duoyi Games' Gunfire Reborn Studio.
community.consensus_summary: Players love it: Steam shows about 93% positive across roughly 104k reviews (Very Positive), and Steam Spy puts owners at 2-5 million. Praise centres on satisfying gunplay, character and weapon variety, and strong co-op. Critics are more lukewarm: the Metacritic page (Xbox version) has a 75 critic score from 10 reviews and a 7.1 user score from 64 ratings. It launched in early access in May 2020, reached 1.0 in Nov 2021 and later came to consoles and mobile. It is still updated, with seasonal content and paid DLC characters about every six months. Recent Steam negatives focus on DLC power creep, machine-translated text, dead co-op matchmaking, suspected AI-generated art and an EULA change.
best_things: Gunplay is fun and satisfying, often compared to Borderlands and Immortal Redneck, with an addictive run loop
Large roster of characters, each with two skills and an ultimate, that change how a run plays, especially in co-op
Wide variety of weapons and scrolls allows many build experiments, including lucky-shot and elemental builds
Bosses are distinct and fluid, each with readable mechanics
Great character designs, from cool to cute, in a colourful art style
Co-op networking is smooth, and each player gets their own drops that can be traded
Seasonal mechanics are all kept available so players avoid FOMO, and support continues years after release
worst_things: English localization is widely described as machine-translated, with confusing or wrong descriptions and some text left in Chinese
DLC characters are much stronger than base ones, making runs on the highest difficulty very easy and creating power creep
Build variety becomes stale, with each character reduced to a few optimal weapon and skill combos, and seasonal mechanics feel similar
Online co-op matchmaking is described as dead, so co-op needs friends
Balance swings in high difficulty, where enemies either die in one hit or barely take damage
Recent reviews cite undisclosed AI-generated art in official artwork and emotes, which drove a wave of negative reviews
Some players report worsening performance, crashes and lost save data over time
New EULA added forced arbitration and deletion of data after 365 days of inactivity, drawing the most-upvoted recent negative reviews even from fans
improvements: Add more bosses per stage and new stage areas, since current boss variety is limited
Make updates meatier, because long-term players say a year of patches can be seen in a few hours and maxing meta progression is quick
Improve English localization and tooltips so item and scroll interactions are clear
Rebalance DLC versus base characters and give hard difficulties a real challenge ceiling
Fix matchmaking or add a lobby or social hub for co-op players
Offer a clearer dodge (short distance and unclear i-frames) and possible third-person or mod support, both requested by players
unique_things: Hades-and-Borderlands-style mix: FPS shooting with hero abilities, scroll (passive) builds and Chinese mythology-inspired anthropomorphic characters
Scroll system lets players assemble synergies, with each character having a different preferred approach (cat for elements, owl for scrolls, fox for frontal assault)
Seasons as switchable, permanently available mechanics with a free battle pass rather than limited-time FOMO
Each co-op player has individual drops, guns and scrolls that can still be exchanged
Runs are long, skill-based dungeon crawls where player skill and enemy knowledge matter more than level-ups
tedious_or_disliked: Runs can feel repetitive in the short term, and veterans say restarting becomes a chore once builds feel samey
Waiting for co-op matches, or never finding one
Getting key scrolls matters for some builds, so a run can be lost to luck of drops
Reading unclear tooltips and untranslated text to understand mechanics
Meta-progression is quickly maxed, leaving little to chase between updates
Dodge feels awkward and the game can feel laggy even solo for some players
divisive_points: DLC model: some see it as fair funding for a live-service game with no FOMO, others see paid characters as power creep and pay-to-win-feeling
Difficulty: early runs feel unfair and punishing, yet experienced players find builds trivial on the hardest difficulty
Comparison to Roboquest, Deadzone Rogue and Abyssus: some say gunplay is weaker but content is larger, others feel its builds are shallower
Update cadence and nerfs: fans praise ongoing support while others call updates thin and dislike character nerfs
community.reception_notes: Early access started May 22, 2020, with 1.0 on Nov 2021 (Steam lists Nov 17, 2021). It had passed 2 million copies by Nov 2021 per Wikipedia, and third-party estimates (Steam Spy 2-5M owners, steam-revenue-calculator about $65.7M gross and about $19.4M net, Boxleiter-method estimates) suggest a large hit. It reached mobile in May 2022, Xbox and PC Game Pass in Oct 2022 and PlayStation in June 2023. Metacritic's 75 and 7.1 come from the console-era page with few ratings. Wikipedia lists the PS and Switch releases, while Metacritic also lists Switch. The Metacritic critic score is based on only 10 reviews. OpenCritic could not be retrieved (web search budget was exhausted and guessed URLs were wrong), so it is left null. Recent Steam reviews (2025-2026) show a mix of long-time fans praising seasons and continued support, and negative reviews over alleged undisclosed AI art, a new EULA with forced arbitration and inactive-data deletion, DLC power creep and nerfs, plus a report that the game pinged a domain the developers no longer control. Steam community threads also mention crashes and data loss. Steam lists Windows only, despite other platforms.
